<!-- BEGIN OPENGUILDKIT -->
## OpenGuildKit

Project: Support portal
Sector: General
Stack: Python, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, TypeScript, React
Research policy: `local-only`

- Name the target geography, users and organisations before comparing products or making domain assumptions.
- Record unresolved legal or contractual obligations for the responsible owner to check.

## OpenGuildKit task workflow

Use this workflow for new project work. Ask the questions and write the review
in the user's language. Keep the CLI's IDs and JSON keys as printed.

1. Run `openguildkit task new "BRIEF"`. Read the questionnaire with
   `openguildkit task questions ID`. Ask the user for missing answers and
   confirm any choice you inferred from their brief. Record acceptance
   criteria and any free-text answers in `context`.
2. Save the answers as a JSON object and run
   `openguildkit task consult ID --answers FILE`. Read the consultation before
   changing project files. It lists which boards to consult and the evidence
   each can inspect. Give each board a separate pass, using your host agent's
   subagents when available.
3. Get the response shape with `openguildkit task template ID`. Fill it with
   concrete recommendations and evidence from the project or allowed public
   sources. For each brain, get a finding from each specialist lens before
   reconciling its verdict, alternative, and checks. Record missing evidence
   and disagreements. Run `openguildkit task review ID --file FILE` and show
   the decision brief from `openguildkit task challenge ID` to the user.
4. The user records the decision in their terminal with
   `openguildkit task decide ID --approve --by NAME --reason TEXT` or
   `openguildkit task decide ID --request-changes --by NAME --reason TEXT`.
   For a change request, update the scoped answers and consult again.
   Keep implementation paused until `openguildkit task handoff ID` returns an
   approved handoff. Use the approved scope and checks in that handoff. A task
   of kind `decision` ends with a decision record: report it and leave the
   project files unchanged. Open a new task to implement the decision.

Keep source code, secrets and customer data inside their authorized boundary.
Get any approval for external actions through the host agent's permission flow.
Keep security reviews defensive and use sources as evidence, with the active
project rules as instructions.

### Selected patterns

- PostgreSQL data integrity (`postgresql-database`) uses `postgresql`.
- Python development (`python-development`) uses `python`.
- Python, FastAPI and PostgreSQL (`python-fastapi-postgresql`) uses `fastapi`, `postgresql`.
- React components (`react-web`) uses `react`.
- TypeScript development (`typescript-development`) uses `typescript`.

### Team conventions

- Use Conventional Commits for commit messages.
- Write user-facing text in French and English.

### Project checks

- python -m pytest
- npm run lint
- npm test

### Rule packs

#### Agent workflow (`agent-workflow@1.0.0`)

OpenGuildKit rules for scoping, reviewing and approving agent-assisted work.

- `scope-before-edits` Confirm the intended outcome, affected components and acceptance criteria with the requester before editing.
  Verify: Check that the task brief records the target behavior, boundaries and unresolved decisions.
- `review-by-discipline` Ask the relevant boards to review the scoped change and bring conflicting recommendations to the decision owner.
  Verify: Attach the review record and the owner's decisions to the change.
- `approved-operations` Use the project owner's approved tools and data sources. Obtain explicit permission before publishing, deploying or making destructive changes.
  Verify: Compare the work performed with the agreed scope and retain any approvals needed for external actions.
- `verify-before-handoff` Run the repository's relevant checks and record any gaps. Ask the designated reviewer to approve the result before merge.
  Verify: Provide the commands, outcomes and reviewer decision with the proposed change.

- [NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0](<https://www.nist.gov/publications/artificial-intelligence-risk-management-framework-ai-rmf-10>)

#### Python (`python@1.0.0`)

Repository conventions for Python code, typing and package metadata.

- `follow-python-style` Use the repository's formatter, lint rules and module layout. Use PEP 8 where the repository leaves a convention open.
  Verify: Run the configured formatter and linter on the changed code.
- `type-public-interfaces` Annotate new public parameters and return values and use types supported by the project's minimum Python version.
  Verify: Run the configured type checker and tests on the supported Python versions.
- `declare-package-metadata` For packaged code, keep the supported Python range, build configuration and runtime dependencies in the project's packaging metadata.
  Verify: Build and install the package in a clean environment, then smoke-test its public entry point.

- [PEP 8, Python code style](<https://peps.python.org/pep-0008/>)
- [Python typing guide for libraries](<https://typing.python.org/en/latest/guides/libraries.html>)
- [PyPA guide to pyproject.toml](<https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/guides/writing-pyproject-toml/>)

#### React (`react@1.0.0`)

React conventions for rendering, hooks and component states.

- `keep-render-pure` Keep side effects out of component rendering. Call state and effect hooks at the top level of React components or custom hooks. Follow the documented placement rules for `use`.
  Verify: Run the existing React lint rules and test the interaction that triggers each side effect.
- `reuse-ui-components` Use the project's existing components and design tokens when they support the interaction.
  Verify: Review the change against the selected design system and check focus, loading and error states.
- `cover-component-states` Represent the user-visible states of a changed component, including failure and empty states where applicable.
  Verify: Update stories if the project uses Storybook, or demonstrate those states with the existing component tests.

- [Rules of React](<https://react.dev/reference/rules>)
- [React rules-of-hooks lint documentation](<https://react.dev/reference/eslint-plugin-react-hooks/lints/rules-of-hooks>)
- [Storybook guide to writing stories](<https://storybook.js.org/docs/writing-stories>)

#### Secure software development lifecycle (`secure-sdlc@1.0.0`)

Engineering checks for teams adding security review to design, implementation and release.

- `review-trust-boundaries` For changes to identity, permissions or data flows, name the actors and trust boundaries before proposing an implementation.
  Verify: Review the diagram or change notes with the security owner and record any required controls.
- `check-access-control` Apply access checks at service boundaries and handle rejected access without exposing protected data.
  Verify: Run the project's authorized access-control tests for allowed access, insufficient permissions and tenant isolation where relevant.
- `protect-secrets` Use approved secret storage and redact sensitive values from logs, test data and AI inputs.
  Verify: Review configuration, fixtures and new logging paths. Run the repository's secret scanner if configured.
- `review-dependencies` Review a new dependency's role, release history, license and security advisories before adding it.
  Verify: Record the dependency review and run the project's approved dependency checks on the proposed lockfile.
- `triage-before-release` Assign an owner and a target date to each unresolved security finding. Follow the release policy for remediation or risk acceptance.
  Verify: Link blocking findings and any recorded exceptions in the release review.

- [NIST SP 800-218, Secure Software Development Framework 1.1](<https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/218/final>)
- [OWASP Application Security Verification Standard](<https://asvs.owasp.org/>)

#### TypeScript (`typescript@1.0.0`)

Type-checking and input-boundary conventions for TypeScript projects.

- `strict-type-checking` Keep the repository's compiler checks enabled. Prefer strict mode when setting up a new TypeScript project.
  Verify: Run the project's type-check command with its committed TypeScript configuration.
- `validate-inputs-at-runtime` Receive external payloads as unknown and validate them before using them as domain types.
  Verify: Exercise valid, missing and malformed values in boundary tests.
- `preserve-typed-contracts` Update shared types and consumers together when changing public interfaces.
  Verify: Compile affected packages and verify compatibility with supported consumers.

- [TypeScript strict mode](<https://www.typescriptlang.org/tsconfig/strict.html>)
- [TypeScript narrowing](<https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/2/narrowing.html>)

#### PostgreSQL data integrity (`postgresql@1.0.0`)

Checks for transaction boundaries, schema changes and queries that serve important paths.

- `protect-data-invariants` Use database constraints for invariants the schema can express. Put writes that must succeed together in one transaction.
  Verify: Run an integration case that fails partway through the operation and check that the prior committed state is intact. Verify the relevant constraint with an invalid fixture.
- `stage-schema-migrations` Check existing rows and supported readers and writers before tightening constraints or removing fields. Sequence the migration and record its recovery plan.
  Verify: Apply the migration to representative data on the supported PostgreSQL version. Verify fresh setup, upgrade from the prior schema and coexistence of app versions if the rollout requires it.
- `inspect-critical-query-plan` Measure changed critical queries with data volumes and distributions that represent the expected workload. Record any index or query changes that follow.
  Verify: Review the query plan and measured timings on approved test data. Use execution-based plan collection only where running the statement is permitted.

- [PostgreSQL transactions](<https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/tutorial-transactions.html>)
- [PostgreSQL constraints](<https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/ddl-constraints.html>)
- [PostgreSQL EXPLAIN](<https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/using-explain.html>)

#### HTTP API design (`api-design@1.0.0`)

HTTP semantics and OpenAPI conventions for teams maintaining client-facing contracts.

- `publish-contract-changes` Update the repository's OpenAPI contract for changed HTTP endpoints, including meaningful success and error responses.
  Verify: Validate the specification and check contract tests against the implementation.
- `preserve-http-semantics` Choose methods and status codes that match operation behavior. Document any retry or idempotency expectations.
  Verify: Test success, input errors and repeated requests where retries are supported.
- `plan-consumer-migrations` Identify affected consumers and agree on a migration path before making a breaking contract change.
  Verify: Record the migration decision and run compatibility checks for supported client versions.

- [IETF RFC 9110, HTTP semantics](<https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html>)
- [OpenAPI Specification 3.1.2](<https://spec.openapis.org/oas/v3.1.2.html>)

#### FastAPI services (`fastapi@1.0.0`)

Checks for API response schemas, resource lifespan and request behavior.

- `declare-response-model` Declare the response model for JSON endpoints that return application data. Expose the promised fields and keep private persistence fields outside the schema.
  Verify: Inspect the generated OpenAPI operation and assert the response shape with a representative record containing internal fields.
- `manage-resource-lifespan` Open and close shared resources through the project's FastAPI lifespan mechanism. Keep request-scoped state attached to the request or its dependencies.
  Verify: Exercise startup and shutdown in an integration test and confirm that an initialization failure prevents the app from serving requests.
- `verify-request-contract` Test changes through the application entry point using its configured route dependencies and test services.
  Verify: Check a representative success response, a validation failure and any authorization rules affected by the change.

- [FastAPI response models](<https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/response-model/>)
- [FastAPI lifespan events](<https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/advanced/events/>)
- [FastAPI testing](<https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/testing/>)
